guarantees.claim: state_we is continuously assigned to sp2v_sig_chk[0].
key_full_we is continuously assigned to sp2v_sig_chk[1].
key_dec_we is continuously assigned to sp2v_sig_chk[2].
sp_enc_err_d is the bitwise OR of sp2v_sig_err, sub_bytes_err, and key_expand_err.

assumptions.claim: sp2v_sig_chk bits are correctly asserted by the upstream sparse checker only when the corresponding sparse signals are valid, providing glitch-free enable signals.
assumptions.risk: A spurious pulse on sp2v_sig_chk[0..2] can cause unintended assertion of state_we, key_full_we, or key_dec_we, leading to state or key corruption.

assumptions.claim: sp2v_sig_err, sub_bytes_err, key_expand_err are valid, stable error flags (no metastability, no false assertion) and reflect actual sparse encoding violations.
assumptions.cond: when errors may occur and sp_enc_err_d is sampled
assumptions.risk: A spuriously high error flag asserts sp_enc_err_d, potentially triggering unnecessary fault handling and masking real errors.

uncertain_points.claim: The write enable signals state_we, key_full_we, key_dec_we depend solely on the sparse-to-vector checker driving sp2v_sig_chk; any fault or misconnection in that checker could cause incorrect enables.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect state or key updates may compromise cipher operation or leak key material.

uncertain_points.claim: The aggregated error signal sp_enc_err_d relies on sub_bytes_err and key_expand_err from other checkers; if these are not connected or silent, sparse encoding errors will not be detected.
uncertain_points.risk: Undetected sparse encoding faults can propagate, corrupting cipher state or exposing secret data.
